task.description:
Closing REVIEWER gate on WF-03 / ISS-0200. Two things are under review and they are not the same object -- gate BOTH, and say so separately in your verdict:

(1) THE NO-CHANGE VERDICT ITSELF, at handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-005-01-diagnose.json. This is the unusual part of this gate and the reason it exists. core-directives.md's "every producing step has a validating step" is not suspended by a producing step concluding "no defect" -- an unvalidated NO-CHANGE is exactly the shape of an unchecked claim, and it is the shape most likely to be waved through, because nothing changed. Step 1 itself asked for this gate.

(2) THE EDIT, commit 69fc2a1, at handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-03-record-verdict.json. Three files: docs/agents/protocols/ISSUE_QUEUE.md, docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md, docs/issues/ISS-0191.yaml.

Both handoffs state their evidence and quote their own commands. Re-derive; do not copy. core-directives.md's "Re-derive under the conditions the property is actually about" binds here: a check run where the property could not have failed is not evidence.

ON (1) -- WHAT TO ACTUALLY TEST. The verdict rests on three legs, and the diagnosis says openly that the first is weak on its own. Your job is to decide whether they hold TOGETHER, not to re-run the whole measurement.
  - The shingle figures. The diagnosis reports its own calibration against the known-true-positive dispatch population (max 0.347) and concludes the numbers are load-bearing only COMPARATIVELY. Check that reasoning survives -- and specifically, check that the comparison is between comparable populations rather than between two differently-constructed ones.
  - Evidence density and the hand-read of the worst-scoring large summary. Read that summary yourself if you doubt it; it is named in the diagnosis.
  - The asymmetry argument (the dispatch defect had a duplicated copy AND an empty structured outlet; neither exists on the result side). This is the load-bearing conceptual claim. `requirement_text` empty in 66 of 69 was the dispatch-side evidence -- check whether the result-side counterpart claim (`artifacts_out` non-empty on 449 of 605) actually establishes what it is being used to establish, given ISS-0202's finding that 190 of those 449 are self-referential. ORCH flags this as the single most likely soft spot and did not resolve it.
A verdict of "the measurement is sound but the conclusion overreaches" is a legitimate FAIL and is more useful than a pass.

ON (2) -- ISS-0200's AC4 IS THE HARD ONE and it is verifiable: HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 4's validator-re-derivation requirement and section 2's four worked examples must be byte-identical to their pre-edit state. Step 3 quotes sha256 spans and a 0-deletions numstat; re-derive that independently, by your own method, against the merge-base rather than against Step 3's arithmetic.
Also gate: that the new section-2 block cannot be read as a rule or as stating a threshold (this is the whole risk of recording a negative result in a rules document -- a later agent citing it as a size constraint is the failure mode); that no WARN or threshold was added anywhere; that the 6,000 threshold is still declared in exactly one place; that (B)(ii) and (C) say the same thing and cannot drift; that the new `no_defect` status does not weaken what `resolved` asserts and that its evidence bar genuinely cannot be met by an uninvestigated issue; and that section 2's JSON fence still parses.

SCOPE: gate only. Change no file except your own handoff. If you find a defect, FAIL with the specific gap named per file and line -- do not fix it yourself. If you find something real but non-gating, put it in result.issues at MINOR and let it be filed, as the ISS-0198 gate did; do not absorb it into a PASS silently.
ORCH's own two notes for you, neither pre-decided: DOC-UPDATER recorded its status-name reasoning (`no_defect` over `no_change`/`not_reproduced`) in result.issues -- rule on it. And Step 3 landed as TWO commits, 69fc2a1 (content) then 574c91d, the second recording the first's sha into its own git_evidence, on the ground that a sha cannot be recorded inside the commit it names. Rule on whether that is the right mechanism -- HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 5's append-only rule and section 4.1(b)'s `backfill_note` are the relevant provisions, and WF03-ISS0198-20260821's commit 3b845b3 is the precedent.
acceptance_criteria: A verdict on the NO-CHANGE verdict itself, stated separately from the verdict on the edit, naming which of its three legs you re-derived and how
An explicit ruling on whether `artifacts_out` non-empty on 449/605 establishes the asymmetry claim it is used for, given that ISS-0202 measured 190 of those 449 as self-referential

ISS-0200 AC4 re-derived independently against the merge-base by your own method, not by checking Step 3's arithmetic: section 4's re-derivation requirement and section 2's four worked examples byte-identical
A ruling that the new section-2 block cannot be read as a rule or as stating a threshold, quoting the wording that makes that unambiguous
Confirmed: no WARN and no threshold added anywhere; the 6,000 threshold still declared in exactly one place; (B)(ii) and (C) consistent
A ruling on whether `no_defect`'s evidence bar can be met by an issue nobody investigated, and on the status name itself
Section 2's JSON fence still parses (your own check, not Step 3's)
A ruling on whether Step 3 two-commit sha-recording mechanism (69fc2a1 then 574c91d) is the authorised way to record a commit sha into its own handoff, against section 5 and section 4.1(b)
No file modified except this handoff (quote git status --porcelain)

result.summary:
WF-03 Step 3b -- closing REVIEWER gate on ISS-0200. TWO OBJECTS GATED SEPARATELY, as dispatched.

VERDICT (1) THE NO-CHANGE VERDICT ITSELF (step-005-01-diagnose.json): PASS. All three legs re-derived first-hand; the conclusion survives.
VERDICT (2) THE EDIT (69fc2a1, three files): FAIL. ONE BLOCKER, one line: docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md:287. Everything else in the edit passes, including ISS-0200 AC4, which I re-derived independently against merge-base 7322185 and confirm.

Overall result.status = FAIL because the edit does not pass. The NO-CHANGE verdict is NOT the thing failing, and rework must not disturb it.

=== VERDICT (1) -- THE NO-CHANGE VERDICT: PASS ===
Re-derived, not copied. Corpus re-measured with my own scripts (scratch/rev0200.py, scratch/rev_dens.py, scratch/rev_shingle.py; scratch/ is git-ignored, so the method is described here in full and the figures below are mine, not Step 1's).

My corpus: n=607 parseable, 0 unparseable (Step 1 had 605; the delta is this run's own two later handoffs, the expected growth). len(result.summary) median 3,005 / p90 8,571 / p95 12,347 / max 47,036 / total 2,622,755. len(task.description) median 710 / p90 3,962 / p95 5,737 / max 19,040 / total 898,232. Pooled ratio 2.920x. Per-handoff ratio n=603, median 3.52x, p90 13.86x, max 43.48x. summ>6000: 122; desc>6000: 26. Every one of Step 1's figures reproduces within the two-file growth. No disagreement to report under HANDOFF_PROTOCOL section 1.1.

LEG A -- THE SHINGLE FIGURES, AND THE COMPARABILITY OF THE POPULATIONS. Re-derived by writing my own 8-gram overlap independently (lowercased [a-z0-9_]+ tokenisation, k=8, scored as |summary_shingles AND source_shingles| / |summary_shingles|, source = concatenated on-disk content of the files named in the handoff's own artifacts_in, handoff JSON excluded). Results on the ONE axis where the two sides are directly comparable -- same axis, same corpus, same method:
    RESULT big summaries vs artifacts_in      n=120  median 0.017  p90 0.089  max 0.262  (argmax handoffs/WF03-ISS0106-20260821/step-015-reviewer-decision-signoff.json)
    DISPATCH big descriptions vs artifacts_in n=26   median 0.023  p90 0.120  max 0.396  (argmax handoffs/ADHOC-20260821-002/step-01-workflow-rules.json)
Step 1 reported 0.264 / 0.167 and 0.347 / 0.200 on the same pair. My independent implementation reproduces the DIRECTION and the magnitudes; the small numeric drift is tokenisation, not substance. The comparative form of the claim -- the result side scores at or below the side already ruled acceptable in its non-restated part -- holds under a second implementation.

ON THE COMPARABILITY OF THE TWO POPULATIONS, which the dispatch asked me to check specifically: they are NOT identically constructed, and Step 1 says so itself (6,000 selects 4.3% of descriptions but 19.8% of summaries -- "large" means the extreme tail on one side and the norm on the other). I ruled on whether that breaks the inference and it does not, for a reason Step 1 did not state and I am stating: the non-comparability runs in the CONSERVATIVE direction. The result population is 4.6x larger (120 vs 26) and less extreme within its own distribution, so it has strictly more opportunity to throw a high maximum -- and it still produced a LOWER one. A larger, less-selected population failing to beat a smaller, more-selected one's ceiling is evidence for the verdict, not a confound in it. Leg A survives, in its comparative form only, exactly as Step 1 scoped it.

LEG B -- EVIDENCE DENSITY AND THE HAND-READ. Re-derived with my own density metric (segments >25 chars split on '.' and newline; a segment counts if it carries a digit, a path-like token, or an identifier of the form ABC-123). My figures: 122 large summaries, median 0.724, p10 0.600, min 0.467; 26 large descriptions, median 0.644, min 0.337. Absolute values differ from Step 1's (0.653 / 0.367) because my regex is looser -- but the DIRECTIONAL claim, which is the one the verdict actually uses, reproduces under an independently written metric: large summaries are more evidence-dense than large descriptions, and the floor is far from zero. Restatement would dilute that ratio; it is instead the highest in the corpus.
I READ THE NAMED HARD CASE MYSELF: handoffs/WF02-REQ027-20260816/step-02c-security-reviewer.json, 34,681 chars. It opens by re-deriving ORCH's scope test in terms ("re-derived, not inherited from ORCH"), verifies the dispatch's own diff listing against the actual diff rather than taking it on trust, and carries per-invariant INV-1..INV-8 determinations. Its artifacts_in are seven .ex/.exs/.md files and it restates none of them. Step 1's characterisation of this file is accurate. Leg B holds.

LEG C -- THE ASYMMETRY ARGUMENT. This is where the failure is. The CONCEPTUAL claim passes; one STATISTIC used to support it does not, and it was carried into HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md verbatim. See AC2 below and BLOCKER-1. The conceptual claim -- a duplicated copy has a source it drifts from, an attestation IS the source, and section 4 makes the acting agent the only party who can write it -- is sound, and is not what fails.

WHY (1) IS STILL A PASS DESPITE LEG C's DEFECT: the NO-CHANGE conclusion does not rest on the defective statistic. It rests on M1's direct measurement over the pairs that actually exist, on the structural attestation argument, and on legs A and B. Strike the 449-of-605 sentence entirely and the verdict is unchanged. The defect is in a supporting sentence that was then written into a canonical protocol document -- which is why it fails the EDIT and not the VERDICT.

=== AC2 -- EXPLICIT RULING: DOES `artifacts_out` NON-EMPTY ON 449/605 ESTABLISH THE ASYMMETRY CLAIM? ===
NO. It does not. Ruled against on two independent grounds. This is BLOCKER-1.

(i) THE NUMBER IS INFLATED, AND THE RUN KNEW IT. Measured first-hand, treating an artifacts_out entry whose basename equals the handoff file's own basename as a self-reference: of 607 handoffs, 450 have a non-empty artifacts_out; 191 of those contain a self-reference; and 115 of them contain NOTHING BUT self-references. Handoffs carrying at least one genuine non-self artefact: 335 of 607 (55%), not 449 of 605 (74%). Restricted to the population actually under test -- the 122 summaries over 6,000 chars -- only 43 of 122 (35%) name any genuine produced artefact at all. ISS-0202, filed by the SAME agent in the SAME run at 09:59:25Z, measured 190 of 449 self-referential and states in terms that "the self-references are noise in that population." The contaminated figure was written into HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md anyway, without that qualification. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 1.1 -- in the very document being edited -- says a checkable factual premise that re-measurement contradicts is corrected, not carried forward. That rule was not applied to the run's own number.

(ii) EVEN AT ITS CORRECT VALUE IT IS THE WRONG INSTRUMENT, AND IT POINTS THE OTHER WAY. The claim it is asked to carry is "there is no result-side field sitting empty while its content rides in prose," offered as the counterpart to `requirement_text == {}` in 66 of 69. Those are not comparable objects. `requirement_text` empty measured a field whose content DEMONSTRABLY EXISTED elsewhere (requirements.yaml) and was found inlined in prose -- emptiness there is evidence of a suppressed outlet. `artifacts_out` non-empty is a raw presence count over ALL handoffs, including gate and decision steps that correctly produce no artefact; an empty artifacts_out on a gate is not a suppressed outlet, it is an accurate report of nothing produced. Opposite polarity, different denominators, differently-constructed populations. And read at face value, the CORRECTED number would appear to support the very condition it is cited to refute: 65% of large summaries have no genuine structured outlet.
What actually defeats the empty-outlet analogy is STRUCTURAL, not numerical, and Step 1 already has it two sentences later: a result.summary has no pre-existing artefact whose content could ride in prose -- prose attestation is not a file that was suppressed. That argument stands alone. The count adds nothing to it and imports a known-contaminated statistic into a canonical document.

REMEDY (named, not implemented -- this is a gate): at docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md:287, either strike the clause "`artifacts_out` is non-empty on 449 of 605 handoffs, and" so the sentence begins "Where it points at a real produced artefact...", or replace the figure with the self-reference-corrected one AND the qualification, citing ISS-0202. The M1 clause that follows ("where it points at a real produced artefact the summary does not duplicate it", n=35, max 0.264) is sound and must be kept, as must the attestation argument at 288-291. Nothing else in that paragraph needs to move.

=== VERDICT (2) -- THE EDIT, 69fc2a1: FAIL (one BLOCKER); all other criteria PASS ===

AC3 -- ISS-0200 AC4, RE-DERIVED INDEPENDENTLY AGAINST THE MERGE-BASE BY MY OWN METHOD: CONFIRMED. I did not check Step 3's arithmetic. Method: extract the named spans from `git show 7322185:docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` and from HEAD by heading regex, hash each with sha256. Results (first 16 hex):
    "### Worked examples" .. "## 3."          7322185 0395b8841ae1169c (4,820 chars)   HEAD 0395b8841ae1169c (4,820)   IDENTICAL
    "## 4. Complete the handoff" .. "## 5."   7322185 db64c4d70402e39d (25,597 chars)  HEAD db64c4d70402e39d (25,597)  IDENTICAL
    "## 4.1" .. "## 5."                       7322185 c5cb5294590c7e0e (23,624 chars)  HEAD c5cb5294590c7e0e (23,624)  IDENTICAL
Section 4's validator-re-derivation requirement (HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md:490, "re-derive your verdict from the artefact itself") sits inside the byte-identical section-4 span. The worked-examples span contains exactly FOUR examples and I counted them by name: validator-fail, validator-pass, security-reviewer-scoped, partial. All four byte-identical.
Corroborating, and independent of the hashes: `git diff --numstat 7322185 HEAD` gives `69  0  docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md` -- zero deletions -- and `git diff -U0 7322185 HEAD` places every insertion hunk at @@ -241,0 +242,54 @@, @@ -853,0 +908,6 @@ and @@ -874,0 +932,9 @@. Section 2's worked examples begin at HEAD:306 and section 4 at HEAD:459; no hunk lands inside either. I checked hunk POSITION as well as deletion count deliberately: with 0 deletions an insertion could still have landed INSIDE a protected span and broken byte-identity, so the numstat alone would not have been sufficient evidence. It did not. PASS.

AC4 -- THE NEW SECTION-2 BLOCK CANNOT BE READ AS A RULE OR AS STATING A THRESHOLD: PASS. The wording that makes it unambiguous, quoted from HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md:242-248:
    "**A MEASURED NEGATIVE RESULT -- NOT A RULE, AND IT STATES NO THRESHOLD.**"
    "**Nothing here constrains the length of any `result.summary`, no target or budget is stated or to be inferred, and this block must not be cited as a size rule.**"
Both are bolded; the first is the block's opening sentence, in capitals; the second forecloses the specific misuse (citation as a size rule) rather than merely denying intent. The block closes at :293 with "no result-side entry in the inline-vs-`artifacts_in` table, no required shape, no length target." A later agent citing this as a size constraint would have to read past three explicit disclaimers, one of which names that exact act. This is the correct handling of the risk the dispatch identified. PASS.

AC5 -- NO WARN, NO THRESHOLD, 6,000 DECLARED ONCE, (B)(ii) AND (C) CONSISTENT: PASS.
  - WARN: every WARN token added by this branch is a NEGATION. `git diff 7322185 HEAD -- docs/ | grep "^+.*WARN"` returns five lines, all of the form "No threshold, no WARN, no pass/fail", "a WARN here would be a length rule by the back door", or a cross-reference to H-SIZE-1's existing dispatch-side WARN. No new WARN was created; H-SIZE-3 remains INFO/never-fails, so no gate changed.
  - 6,000: `grep -rn "6,000\|6000" --include=*.md --include=*.yaml` over docs/ returns four hits in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md (230, 901, 916, 918), all four pre-existing and untouched (0 deletions on the file; none falls inside an added hunk), plus ISS-0198.yaml:105 and ISS-0202.yaml:15. Only 916/918 DECLARE the threshold; 901 is that same block's machine spec of it, and 230 / ISS-0198:105 / ISS-0202:15 are corpus measurements describing a population, not declarations. This edit added ZERO new occurrences: the new section-2 block deliberately refuses to repeat the number, writing "the char count H-SIZE-1's WARN uses on the dispatch side -- stated once, in the Enforcement note, and deliberately not repeated here" and giving only the derived selectivity (4.3% vs 19.8%). Declared in exactly one place. PASS.
  - (B)(ii) at HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md:908-913 and 935-943, and (C) at ISS-0191.yaml:67-80, read side by side: same emit list (median/max/total len(result.summary) plus the per-step summary/description ratio), same REPORT ONLY / no threshold / no WARN / no pass-fail, same back-door reasoning, same does-not-run-today framing. (C) explicitly declines to re-derive the spec -- "Specified in full in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md's Enforcement note ... do not re-derive it here" -- which is the right anti-drift construction: it points at the other rather than duplicating it, so there is no second copy that CAN drift. PASS, and this is the strongest part of the edit.

AC6 -- `no_defect`'s EVIDENCE BAR, AND THE STATUS NAME: PASS on both, ruled explicitly.
  CAN AN UNINVESTIGATED ISSUE MEET THE BAR? No. Ruled by trying to defeat it, not by reading it approvingly. The four MUSTs at ISSUE_QUEUE.md:207-221 are individually unfakeable without work: (1) demands producing code or command QUOTED with real figures, and voids inherited figures by name, so there is nothing to paste from the filing; (2) demands the candidate mechanisms tested, named individually, INCLUDING the ones the data did not support -- this is the one an uninvestigated issue cannot fabricate, because a list of things you looked for and did not find can only be written by someone who looked; (3) demands the method's own limitations, which an agent seeking a cheap exit has neither incentive nor material to write; (4) run-id and timestamp, checkable against handoffs/. The closing sentence forecloses the degenerate case in terms: "a record that says only 'looked, seemed fine' has not reached a terminal status at all -- it is still `open`." And the bar is framed as a positive falsifiable claim ("checked, measured, not there") rather than an absence, so an unbacked `no_defect` is a false statement about reality and misinforms the registry the way a false `resolved` does -- which is the property that makes it self-policing rather than merely strict. `resolved` is untouched: 0 deletions on the file, lines 187-191 unchanged, and the new bullet says so explicitly ("Nothing here relaxes `resolved`'s bar by a hair").
  THE NAME. `no_defect` is right, and I rule for it over DOC-UPDATER's two rejected alternatives -- on DOC-UPDATER's reasoning plus one it did not give. Its reasoning holds: `no_change` names the RUN's action rather than the ISSUE's truth and would read as "we chose not to act", and `not_reproduced` asserts only that one attempt failed, a weaker and different claim. The reason it did not give, and the decisive one: every other value in this vocabulary describes the state of the DEFECT (`open`, `in_progress`, root cause removed, root cause not removed). `no_defect` is the only candidate that stays in that register; `no_change` and `not_reproduced` both describe the run, which would make this the single status in the list whose subject is not the issue. Recording the reasoning in result.issues rather than deciding it silently was the correct call and is the shape this gate wants.

AC7 -- SECTION 2's JSON FENCE PARSES: PASS, my own check. `json.loads` over each ```json fence in the file: fence 0 (the section-2 schema, 2,278 chars) parses OK -- top-level keys handoff_id, run_id, workflow_id, step, from_agent, to_agent, ... The other four fences in the document do not parse standalone and never did: they are the worked examples, each a bare `"result": {...}` fragment, which is a JSON fragment by design, not an object. Those four sit inside the byte-identical span and are unchanged by this edit; I note them only so a later reader running the same check is not misled into thinking this edit broke something. Only fence 0 is declared machine-loadable, and it parses. PASS.

AC8 -- THE TWO-COMMIT SHA-RECORDING MECHANISM (69fc2a1 then 574c91d): RULED AUTHORISED. It is the right mechanism.
  Against section 5 (HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md:841-846): the append-only rule binds `handoffs/orchestrator.log` and `handoffs/registry.json` BY NAME and forbids a commit that REDUCES either file's size. It does not name handoff files, and in any case 574c91d shrinks nothing -- `git show --numstat` gives 3 insertions / 1 deletion, and the single deleted line is `"commit_sha_list": [],` replaced by the same key populated across three lines. Nothing was removed; an empty array was filled. No section 5 conflict.
  Against section 4.1(b): `backfill_note` is NOT the relevant provision and must not be borrowed for this. 4.1(b) governs the CLOSED seven-member `not_agent_attested` marker applied when the acting agent stopped existing, and HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md:682 declares the exception admitting `backfill_note` SPENT -- it authorised one named file. Applying it to a live agent recording its own commit sha would both misuse a spent exception and assert `not_agent_attested` falsely about a handoff its own agent did attest. Correctly not used.
  The underlying argument is simply true: a sha cannot be recorded inside the commit it names, so either it is recorded in a second commit or it is never recorded. The second is worse -- git_evidence.commit_sha_list is what a later reader uses to find the change, and leaving it empty is the ISS-0202 failure mode all over again (a structured field that does not do its one job). Precedent 3b845b3 on WF03-ISS0198-20260821 did exactly this: same shape, one file, additive. Consistent precedent, no rule violated, and the alternative is worse. AUTHORISED. One MINOR filed below: it is authorised by absence of prohibition plus precedent rather than by any positive statement, which invites re-litigation every run.

AC9 -- NO FILE MODIFIED EXCEPT THIS HANDOFF. `git status --porcelain` at completion:
     M handoffs/WF03-ISS0200-20260821/step-03b-reviewer-gate.json
Exactly one line. HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md, ISSUE_QUEUE.md, ISS-0191.yaml and ISS-0200.yaml do not appear. My measurement scripts (rev0200.py, rev_dens.py, rev_shingle.py, rev_fence.py, complete0200.py) live in scratch/, git-ignored per core-directives.md's File Placement Rules. I implemented no fix; BLOCKER-1's remedy is named per file and line above and is left for the owning agent.

=== THE FOUR REVIEWER QUESTIONS, APPLIED TO A DOCS-ONLY CHANGE ===
Idiomatic OTP / :gen_statem: N/A -- no lib/ or priv/repo/migrations/ code in this diff. Supervision integrity: N/A -- no process topology touched. Type-safety gaps: no @type, struct or Ecto.Enum surface changed; the nearest analogue is the issue-status vocabulary, and the new value was added to the canonical list with WF-03 pointed at it rather than restating it, which is the correct direction (see MINOR-1 for the one place that has not caught up). Scope creep: NONE, and worth stating positively -- Step 3 held a NO-CHANGE verdict and declined to write a result-side size rule anyway, which is precisely the abstraction-ahead-of-need this gate exists to catch. The edit records a measurement and closes a vocabulary gap; it builds no machinery. Decision-record consistency: no docs/migration/decisions/ record is touched or contradicted.

issues.description: docs/agents/shared/HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md:287 records a known-contaminated statistic as fact in a canonical protocol document. The sentence reads "`artifacts_out` is non-empty on 449 of 605 handoffs, and where it points at a real produced artefact the summary does not duplicate it." Re-measured first-hand over 607 handoffs: 450 have a non-empty artifacts_out, but 191 contain a self-reference to their own handoff file and 115 contain NOTHING ELSE, so handoffs carrying a genuine non-self artefact number 335 of 607 (55%), not 74%; among the 122 summaries over 6,000 chars -- the population actually under test -- only 43 of 122 (35%) name any genuine produced artefact. ISS-0202, filed by the same agent in the same run at 09:59:25Z, already measured 190/449 self-referential and states the self-references are noise in that population; the figure went into the protocol without that qualification, contrary to HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 1.1's own rule that a re-measurement contradicting a premise wins. Separately, even corrected the count is the wrong instrument: it is a raw presence count over all handoffs including gate steps that correctly produce no artefact, offered as the counterpart to `requirement_text == {}` in 66 of 69, which measured emptiness of a field whose content demonstrably existed elsewhere -- opposite polarity, different denominators, differently-constructed populations -- and read at face value the corrected figure would appear to SUPPORT the empty-outlet condition it is cited to refute. REMEDY: at line 287, strike the clause "`artifacts_out` is non-empty on 449 of 605 handoffs, and" so the sentence begins "Where it points at a real produced artefact...", or replace the figure with the self-reference-corrected one plus the qualification, citing ISS-0202. KEEP the clause that follows it and the attestation argument at 288-291; both are sound and carry the asymmetry claim on their own. Nothing else in the block needs to move, and the NO-CHANGE verdict is unaffected -- do not reopen it.

WF-03 Step 5 has not caught up with the vocabulary it points at. docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md:157-169 hardcodes `status: resolved, resolved_in_run:, resolved_at:` in its Step 5 pseudocode and names only `instrumented` as the legal alternative in the prose that follows. It does correctly defer to ISSUE_QUEUE.md as canonical and says "do not restate them here", so 69fc2a1 introduced no contradiction -- but an agent executing Step 5 by following the pseudocode will write `resolved`, which for this very run is the false statement the new status exists to prevent. Two things go with it: the new bullet requires "the run-id and timestamp" without naming the KEYS a `no_defect` record uses, and `resolved_in_run`/`resolved_at` read wrong on a record that resolved nothing. Recommend WF-03 Step 5's block name `no_defect` as a third legal terminal value, and the ISSUE_QUEUE.md bullet name the key pair a `no_defect` record carries, before ISS-0200 becomes the precedent for both.

The two-commit sha-recording mechanism is authorised (ruled at AC8) but nowhere written down, so it is authorised only by absence of prohibition plus the 3b845b3 precedent. That invites fresh re-litigation every time an agent has to record a content commit's sha into the handoff that produced it -- this gate spent effort on it, ISS-0198's gate spent effort on it, and the next one will too. Recommend one sentence in HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 4 or section 5 stating plainly that a commit sha may be recorded into git_evidence.commit_sha_list by a second, sha-recording-only commit, that this is additive and not a section 5 violation, and that section 4.1(b)'s `backfill_note` does NOT apply because the acting agent is alive and did attest the file.
